title: Optimize All Curve Points
content: **Optimize All Curve Points** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gVIXoamGcT0 \- Easily edit curves by optimizing the number of curve points on segments. Use this function when there are unnecessarily many curve points. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022574027/mceclip0.png) **Edit Curve Point** tool from the 2D toolbar to see all curve points on Patterns. \- Right-click on the 2D window and select **Optimize All Curve Points** from the pop-up menu. Surplus curve points will be deleted and only the necessary curve points needed to maintain the shape of the curves will be remained.
content_description: Learn how to streamline your design process by optimizing curve points in your patterns to enhance editing efficiency and maintain shape integrity.

title: V-Ray Render Image/Video Properties
content: **List of Contents** Image/Video Properties Image/Video Image Size Color Correction Background Save Open/Save Image/Video Properties **Image/Video Properties ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=p-LE9SBjElM \- Select the![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115026473148/mceclip0.png) **Image/Video Properties** tool from the Render toolbar and navigate to the Property Editor. ** Image/Video YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lYoGlUfpf28 ** \- Select the medium for the final Render product among Image, Turntable Images, and Turntable Video. * **Image** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=toGlTvPnjtk \- Extract rendered 3D Garment as an image. * **View Point** * **Current View** \- Render the 3D Garment as it is shown in the 3D window. * **Custom View** \- Render the 3D Garment with a Custom View. * **Render All Colorways** All Colorways from the Colorway Mode are rendered(ver4.1.0). * **Turntable Images ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nuHoLLLoFGY \- Extract rendered 3D Garment as multiple images, showing it in 360°. * **Image Count** \- Decide the number of images to be rendered. \- Higher the Image Count is, from more viewpoints the 3D Garment is rendered. * **Direction** * **Counterclockwise** \- The 3D Garment is rendered counterclockwise. * **Clockwise** \- The 3D Garment is rendered clockwise. * **Render All Colorways** All Colorways from the Colorway Mode are rendered(ver4.1.0). * **Turntable Video** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=I06tDemxstA\- Extract rendered 3D Garment as a video rotating in 360° * **Video Frame Count** \- Decide the number of images to be rendered and stitched as a video. \- Higher the Video Frame Count, more smoothly the video rotates. * **Duration** \- Decide the total duration of the video. \- Expand the child menu to find Video Frame Duration, which decides the duration per frame. * **Direction** * **Counterclockwise** \- The 3D Garment is rendered counterclockwise. * **Clockwise** \- The 3D Garment is rendered clockwise. * **Video Codec** \- Select the video codec used for recording. * **Render All Colorways** All Colorways from the Colorway Mode are rendered(ver4.1.0). **Image Size YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Rf8HfrfQoxE ** \- Set the dimension of rendered images or videos. \- Choose among provided presets or select Custom to freely configure the width and height of the images or videos as needed. * **Orientation** * **Portrait** \- The image is laid out vertically. * **Landscape** \- The image is laid out horizontally. * **Width** \- Set image’s width * **Height** \- Set image’s height * **Maintain Ratio** \- Lock Width and Height ratio by toggling on the Maintain Ratio option. **Color Correction YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mD3iDfUr-bM ** * **Exposure** \- Set how much the image is exposed to light. \- Higher the Exposure value is, brighter the image is. * **Contrast** \- Set how strong the bright and dark areas are contrasted. \- Higher the Contrast value is, stronger the contrast gets. **Background YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_xOG0L70SZ0 ** * **Color** \- Set the color of the background. * **Transparency** \- Set the background image as transparent. **Save YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=D5SSR8rUcKs ** * **File Name** \- Decide the name of the saved images. * **File Path** \- Locate the saving path for the images. **Open/Save Image/Video Properties YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6Jv-fWt1ifY ** * **Open** \- Open previously saved Image/Video Properties. * **Save** \- Save configured Image/Video Properties and apply to other files. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page serves as a comprehensive guide to configuring and rendering image and video properties for 3D garments, complete with instructional videos and detailed options for customization.

title: Linked Editing
content: **List of Contents** Set Linked Editing Remove Linked Editing #### **You can set linked editing to edit the pattern more quickly and efficiently. ** #### **Set Linked Editing** **Symmetric Pattern** 1. Right-click on the pattern to clone it symmetrically with **![Transform Pattern.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/37866981223577)****Transform Pattern** tool. 2. Click on 'Clone Pattern with Linked Editing ▶ **Symmetric Pattern (with Sewing)/Symmetric Pattern'** menu. 3. Click on the 2D window to arragne the clone. **Instance Pattern** 1. Right-click on the pattern to clone it as an instance with **![Transform Pattern.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/37866981223577)Transform Pattern** tool. 2. Click on 'Clone Pattern with Linked Editing ▶**Instance Pattern'** menu. 3. Click on the 2D window to arrange the clone, or right-click on the 2D window while arranging to set the number of shapes and define the interval. **📝****Note:** Right-click on both patterns that are not linked and select the '**Apply Linked Editing** ' menu to apply linked editing without cloning. #### #### **Remove Linked Editing** 1. Right-click on the pattern to remove linked editing with **![Transform Pattern.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/37866981223577)Transform Pattern** tool. 2. Click on the '**Remove Linked Eidting** ' menu. ![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/37866999702937) ### ![Label_Final.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/38097968974361) Linked editing can be removed only for the internal lines within a pattern, while keeping linked editing for the overall pattern. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on how to efficiently use linked editing for symmetric and instance patterns in Clo3D, including step-by-step instructions for setting and removing linked editing.

title: CLO-SET Account Linking
content: **List of Contents** CLO-SET Account Linking Download File **Objective** Download and find the digital contents uploaded on CLO-SET in CLO. **Location** Library ▶ ![Tab.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/33947924285465) CLO-SET Tab **Operation** **CLO-SET Account Linking** 1. Click the tool/menu indicated. 2. Click the CLO-SET Account button at the top right. → The Account window appears. → The method of adding an account is the same as the [CLO-SET CONNECT](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/900005601826) tab. 3. Click the Add Account button. → The CLO-SET Sign In Page appears. 4. Once signed in, return to the CLO interface. → The account is added in the Account window. → The groups you have joined and the favorite folders in CLO-SET appear in the window. ****📝****Note:**** For information on how to use CLO-SET, please click the items below. > • [Favorite Company Library, Workroom or Content](https://support.clo-set.com/hc/en-us/articles/360002197955) > • [Company Library](https://support.clo-set.com/hc/en-us/articles/4409179208335-Company-Library) **Download File** 1. Click the desired item in the CLO-SET tab. →Folders and files within that item appear. 2. Double-click the file to load it. → The file will be loaded. ****📝****Note:**** You can open or [add previous versions of CLO-SET files](https://support.clo-set.com/hc/en-us/articles/360002199235-Content-Version-Upload) directly in CLO by right-clicking on the file thumbnail. (ver 2024.1)
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for linking your CLO-SET account and downloading digital content from CLO.

title: Create POM
content: **List of Contents** Single Group **Objective** Create rulers to check measurements of particular parts of 2D Patterns/Internal Shapes/Graphics. YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BbRGWeNBoq8 **Location** Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Pattern Measure ▶ **Point of Measure** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![pom.jpg](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360039947034) **Point of Measure** **Operation** 1. Select the tool/menu indicated above. ** ** 2. Left-click on a **pattern or internal line** to start creating a ruler. ** ** **Single ** **** 3\. Double click the endpoint or hit Enter to complete creating the ruler. → A single POM is created and added to Object Browser ▶ POM Tab. **Group ** **** 3\. Double click the endpoint or hit Enter to complete creating the ruler. → A group POM is created and added to Object Browser ▶ POM Tab as a single measurement. → The length of the line linking two Patterns (one that is not placed within Patterns) is not included in the measurement. **📝****Note****:** * Hold down the Shift key to display vertical, horizontal, and 45º guidelines based on the clicked point. * To cancel while creating POM, press down the backspace key, ESC or Ctrl+Z (Windows)/Cmd+Z (Mac) keys on the keyboard. * While creating POM, right-click to enter Distance Moved. * Check 3D Length in the Property Editor after creating POM. * Pattern Outlines and Internal Lines can be [traced as POM.](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000307728-Trace) * If there is grading information in the pattern that created the tape measure, the length is displayed by grading size in the POM tab. * When creating a POM, press the **P** key on the keyboard to switch between the mode for generating it along a segment line and the mode for generating it as a polygon.(ver 2024.1) Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on creating rulers for measuring specific parts of 2D patterns and internal shapes in the software, complete with step-by-step instructions and helpful tips.

title: V-Ray Render Light Properties
content: **List of Contents** Light Properties Environment Map Light Intensity Rectangle Light Open/Save Settings **Light Properties YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bFCvu1DpMDw **\- Set lighting properties applied to final render output. \- Select the![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115026363368/mceclip0.png) **Light Properties** tool from the render toolbar and navigate to the Property Editor. ** Environment Map YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=k0o1HqcBmdg **\- The **environment map** is a lighting setting processed into an image format. \- By default, six different environment maps are provided. \- Select the desired environment map as needed. **Light Intensity YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vFTv9Ozi1-U ** \- Adjust the brightness of the 3D Garment in the final rendered image by configuring the Light Intensity. \- The default value is 1.00 and the setting can be adjusted between 0.00 and 4.00. \- Higher the value is, brighter the 3D Garment is. **Rectangle Light YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GFP4F8prd_k ** \- Add and modify point lights up to three. \- Adjust lights' location with the Gizmo tool. * **Intensity ** \- Adjust the intensity of the light. * **Color ** \- Set the color of the light. * **Width ** \- Set the width of the light. * **Height ** \- Set the height of the light. * **Show ** \- Show or hide the light from the 3D window. **※ Note :** * To create a three-dimensional render image, there must be a key light. Add key lights as needed to create more dynamic images. * When the Rectangle Lights are used along with the Dome Light, use a HDRI image without a key light. **Open/Save Settings YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=F2C5rWBwKoI ** * **Open ** \- Click the Open button on the right top corner of the Property Editor to load previously saved Light Properties. * **Save ** \- Click the Save button on the right top corner of the Property Editor to save the configuration. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page serves as a comprehensive guide to configuring and managing lighting properties for 3D garment rendering, including tutorials and tools for adjusting light intensity, environment maps, and saving settings.

title: Transform Pattern
content: **List of Contents** Transform Pattern Select Pattern Select Multiple Patterns Move Pattern Scale Pattern Rotate Pattern **Transform Pattern** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Brn8gLoXpu8 \- Select, move, and scale Patterns. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022750927/mceclip0.png) **Transform Pattern** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- Or, navigate to the Main Menu and select 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ **Tranform Pattern.** ** Select Pattern** * **Click ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Yu35gVF14Ms \- Click within the pattern to be selected. \- Or, create a marquee box to encompass the Patterns to be selected. Keep in mind that the Patterns need to be fully enclosed within the marquee box in order to be selected properly. * **Lasso Selection ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AjMYnBirTVA \- Double click on the 2D window to activate the **Lasso Selection.** \- Click around the Patterns to be selected to draw marquee box in a desired shape and click the start point again the complete the Lasso Selection. \- The selected Patterns will be highlighted in yellow. \- Similar with selecting Patterns with the marquee box, Patterns should be fully enclosed. **Select Multiple Patterns** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZJV_Jha4HY0 \- While selecting Patterns, hold down the Shift key and select all Patterns you desire to select. **Move Pattern** * **With Mouse ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rfuj9xoNSkU \- Click and drag the Pattern. * **With Arrow Keys ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GVUd3GiyxCY \- Click the Pattern to be moved. \- Use the arrow keys on the keyboard to move the Pattern towards the desired direction. \- The Pattern will move in 1cm increments when using the arrow keys on the keyboard. * **Move in Guidelines ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xDPWHJTN2tc \- While click and dragging the Pattern, hold down the Shift key on the keyboard to activate the guidelines. \- The Pattern can be moved in a straight line or a diagonal line. **Scale Pattern** * **Scale Manually ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pfpMEd8QIaU \- Click the Pattern to be scaled. The marquee box will appear around the Pattern. \- Click and drag the white point on the marquee box to enlarge or shrink the selected Pattern. * **Scale with Specific Values ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jYjAxV89Bh8 \- After selecting the Pattern and click and dragging the white point on the marquee box, right click on the 2D window. \- The Transform window will appear. \- Enter the desired values to Percentage and Dimension to scale the Pattern with the desired values. **Rotate Pattern ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=U4Lvim31Bmo \- Click on the Pattern to show the marquee box. \- Click and drag the white point above the marquee box to rotate the selected Pattern. * **Pivot Point** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8HBDKLMnjGg \- The point at the center of the Pattern appears with the marquee box is the Pivot Point. \- Double click the Pivot Point to activate it. 。 \- Move the Pivot Point to change the fiducial point which the Pattern will rotate on the basis of. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page serves as a comprehensive guide for users to learn how to effectively transform, select, move, scale, and rotate patterns within a design software, complete with instructional videos for each function.

title: PBR Map Generator (ver 2024.1)
content: ### **Objective** Generate PBR maps (Normal, Displacement, Opacity, Roughness, Metalness Maps) for realistic texture expresssion from a basic texture image. **Location ** Texture Property Editor ▶ Each PBR Map Properties ▶ ![PBR.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/33852438547481)**PBR Map Generator** ** Operation** 1. Load a texture image from the object properties whose [fabric](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/360047317454-Set-Fabric-Textures) and material you want to change. 2. Select the tool/menu in Location. → Each PBR map is automatically generated based on the texture image.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for generating PBR maps—Normal, Displacement, Opacity, Roughness, and Metalness—from a basic texture image to enhance the realism of your textures in the Texture Property Editor.

title: Create Ellipse
content: **List of Contents** Ellipse Create Ellipse **Ellipse** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OGdaXC2ZLtQ \- Create Ellipse or circle in 2D window. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021379368/mceclip0.png) **Ellipse** tool from the 2D toolbar. ** Create Ellipse** * **Free-hand an Ellipse YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sxHmjZR1yPw ** \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021379368/mceclip0.png) **Ellipse** tool from the 2D toolbar, and then navigate to the 2D window. \- Click and drag on the 2D window as the preview of an Ellipse appears. \- Hold down the Shift key on the keyboard to create a Circle. \- When the desired shape of an Ellipse or a Circle is achieved, release the mouse. \- An Ellipse or a Circle Pattern is created based on the settings. * **Use Diameter & Radius YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6nXIZcSuToE **\- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021379368/mceclip0.png) **Ellipse** tool from the 2D toolbar, and then navigate to the 2D window. ** -** Click on the 2D window. The Create Ellipse Window appears. \- Enter desired values for**Width** ,**Height** , **Diameter** , and**Radius**. Then, hit OK. \- An Ellipse or a Circle Pattern is created based on the settings. * **Use Circumference YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BIpY8PJQ0Zk ** \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021379368/mceclip0.png) **Ellipse** tool from the 2D toolbar, and then navigate to the 2D window. \- Click on the 2D window. The Create Ellipse window appears. \- Enter desired values for **Circumference.** \- An Ellipse or Circle Pattern is created based on the settings. ** ** * **Create and Replicate Ellipses YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7zeIj_wksVg ** \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021379368/mceclip0.png) **Ellipse** tool from the 2D toolbar, and then navigate to the 2D window. \- Click on the 2D window. The Create Ellipse window appears. \- **Interval** : type in the distance between the Ellipses. \- **Angle** : type in the angle that replicated Ellipses will be created. \- **Number of Shapes** : type in the number of Ellipses to be replicated. \- Click OK. \- The Ellipses are created based on the settings above. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page serves as a comprehensive guide for creating and manipulating ellipses and circles in a 2D design environment, featuring step-by-step instructions and instructional YouTube videos for various techniques.

title: Slash and Spread
content: **List of Contents** Slash and Spread Create Slash Line Rotate Pattern **Slash and Spread** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IzVgGn3N-z0 \- Create a Slash Line inside a Pattern to divide, rotate, and edit the Pattern. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022743268/mceclip0.png) **Slash &Spread** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- Or, navigate to the Main Menu and select 2D Patterns ▶ Edit ▶**Slash &Spread.** ** Create Slash Line** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5wzgrEnj0Bk \- To divide and rotate the Patterns, the Slash Line must be created first. \- The Slash Line can be created on the Pattern outlines. \- Click on the Pattern outline to create the start point. The start point of the Slash Line will be the fiducial point where the Pattern will rotated on the basis of. Drag the mouse on click again on the Pattern outline to complete the Slash Line. \- Baselines and Internal Lines can also be used as Slash Lines. 。 **Rotate Pattern** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kYwCxjbo2jU \- Click the half of the Pattern that will be rotated. Hover the mouse over the half and when the Pattern is highlighted in light-blue, click to select. When the half of the Pattern is selected, it will be highlighted in yellow. \- Move the mouse cursor to preview the Pattern after the modification. Rotate the Pattern to spread or clip Patterns. \- Move the half of the Pattern as desired and click to complete the modification. \- Baselines and Internal Lines can also be used to rotate Patterns. \- Or, when moving the half of the Pattern, right-click to access the Spread window. Enter the desired values to Distance and Angle and click OK. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides step-by-step instructions and video tutorials for using the Slash and Spread tool in pattern editing, including creating slash lines and rotating patterns.

title: Add Point/Split Line
content: **List of Contents** Add Point/Split Line Add Point Split into Two Lines Split by Length Uniform Split **Add Point/ Split Line** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aMFIJW6sv-E \- Add point to Pattern outlines and Internal Lines to split them. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021155167/mceclip0.png) **Add Point/Split Line** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- Or, navigate to Main Menu and select 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ **Add Point/Split Line.** ** Add Point** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=91_mK0K3IAs \- Add point to Pattern outlines. \- Add point to Internal Lines. **Split into Two Lines** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4pM4RxsazPo \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021155167/mceclip0.png) **Add Point/ Split Line** tool from the 2D toolbar. Then, right click on a segment and select **Split. ** \- The Split Line window will appear. Click **Split into Two Lines. ** \- The selected line will be divided into two different length segments on the basis of the purple guide point. The desired length can be entered in the Line 1, the shorter segment and the Line 2, the longer segment. \- The selected line will be divided into two different length segments on the basis of the purple guide point. The proportion of each segment can be entered in the Line 1, the shorter segment and the Line 2, the longer segment. **Split by Length** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_iPcukEJ8Qg \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021155167/mceclip0.png) **Add Point/ Split Line** tool from the 2D toolbar. Then, right click on a segment and select **Split. ** \- The Split Line window will appear. Click **Split by Length. ** \- **Segment Length** : points will be added to the line with the Segment Length Interval, starting from one side of the line. \- **Number of Segments** : set how many segments the line will be divided into. \- **Direction** : set toward which direction the points will be added. **Uniform Split** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9Cm0Jkt2zWc \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021155167/mceclip0.png) **Add Point/Split Line** tool from the 2D toolbar. Then, right click on a segment and select **Split. ** \- The Split Line window will appear. Click **Uniform Split. ** \- **Number of Segments** : set how many segments the line will be equally divided into. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page serves as a comprehensive guide for utilizing the **Add Point/Split Line** tool in 2D pattern editing, offering step-by-step instructions and helpful video tutorials for various splitting techniques.

title: Edit Piping
content: **List of Contents** Edit Piping Select Piping Edit Length Edit Piping Properties Piping Right Click Pop-Up Menu **Edit Piping** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HRlB8hFZNTs \- Select and edit Pipings on 3D Garments. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022123967/mceclip0.png) **Edit Piping** tool from the 3D toolbar. \- Or, navigate to and select Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Piping ▶ **Edit Piping** ** ****Select Piping** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7nwPB8rv1Wc \- With the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022123967/mceclip0.png) **Edit Piping** tool selected, click on the Piping on the 3D Garment. \- The selected Piping will be highlighted in yellow. **Edit Length** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JKQ29x65b0U \- With the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022123967/mceclip0.png) **Edit Piping** tool selected, click and drag either end of the Piping towards the direction it will be abridged or extended. **Edit Piping Properties** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yCOxCmFtHQ0 \- With the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022123967/mceclip0.png) **Edit Piping** tool or the **Select/Move** , click the Piping on the 3D Garment and navigate the Property Editor. \- The selected Piping’s properties will appear. * **Name** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NF2_-Uczhwg \- View and edit the name of the selected Piping. * **Line Length** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Z49uvAdpb60 \- View the length of the selected Piping. * **Width** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kZ-t0unGSfE \- View the length of the selected Piping. * **Particle Distance** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qsXXaznbDaQ \- View and edit the Particle Distance of the selected Piping. \- The Piping’s Particle Distance is set as 1.5mm by default. \- Narrower the Piping’s width is, smaller the Particle Distance should be. * **Hide** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qhYY4v5MaHw \- Toggle on or off the **Hide** checkbox to hide or show the selected Piping. \- The Piping will appear translucent when the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022123967/mceclip0.png) **Edit Piping** tool is activated, but it will disappear when other 3D tools are activated. * **Fabric** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Hes_dZzaufc \- Change the fabric material for the selected Piping. \- ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022123967/mceclip0.png) **Edit Piping** tool or the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022184048/mceclip1.png) title: Grainline
content: ## **New in 2024.2** **** **List of Content** **Grain Direction** **Link All Colorways** **Grain Orientation** **Grainline Lock** #### **Adjust the direction and orientation of the grainline, while also being able to lock Grainline properties and adjustments across all modes and features within CLO. ** 1. Click the 2D pattern using the ![Transform Pattern On.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/37931791249049)**Transform Pattern** or ![Edit Pattern On.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/37931791261337)**Edit Pattern** tool in the 2D toolbar. 2. Adjust the direction and orientation of the grainline in the Property Editor. ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/37932578723609) ** ** **Grain Direction** | The main angle/ degree for the pattern's placement on the fabric roll. 1) Click the text field. 2) Press the arrow keys on the keyboard to change the degree based on how the Grain Orientation is set up. Examples: • Grain Orientation One way: The numbers will switch every 45 degrees. • Grain Orientation Two Or Four Way: The numbers will switch every 90 Degrees. 3) Or enter a specific degree. ---|--- **Link All Colorways** | If there are multiple colorways within the project file checking this checkbox on will apply the grainline information to all colorways. If the checkbox is unchecked that means each colorway can be different. ****📝****Note:****_This could be helpful if you want more control when entering production or if you are planning on having different fabrics for different colorways._ **Grain ****Orientation** | To decide how many different orientations/ directions the pattern can be placed on the fabric roll. **📝 Note:**_These options are very important for when moving into production and learning how much it would cost to produce the garment. This is also very important because based on the fabric you have applied certain the different orientations will change how much or how little stretch the garment has._ ** One Way ** | The pattern should only be placed in that one orientation that is dictated by the Grain Direction degree. ** Two Way ** | The pattern can be placed in two different orientation. The degree dictated by the Grain Direction and the degree that is the direct opposite (_180 degree from the original_). Examples: • 0 Degree Original: 180 Degree second option. • 90 Degree Original: 270 Degree Second option. ** Four Way ** | The pattern can be placed in four different orientations. The degree dictated by the Grain Direction and any other orientation that 90 degree from the original degree. Examples: • 0 Degree Original: 90,180,270 other options. • 45 Degree Original: 135,225,315 other options. **Grainline Lock** | Checking this on will lock the grainline across all modes of CLO. Stopping any adjustments to the grainline when working with other tools or functions within CLO that can adjust the Grainline. ****📝****Note:****_This locking is very helpful to keep continuity across all of CLO._ _The Print Layout mode and the Edit Texture tools will be the parts of CLO that are affected the most when checking this on or off._ * *
content_description: Explore the new features of CLO 2024.2, including enhanced grain direction control, orientation options, and the ability to lock grainline properties for consistent garment production.

title: Seam Taping
content: **Reinforce edges of Patterns to withstand from drooping down by gravity when Simulating.** 1. Click on the ![Seam Taping On.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/37880812122905) **Seam Taping** tool on the 2D toolbar. 2. Select a segment Pattern to reinforce, or Click-and-drag also allows applying seam tapes. 3. Activate the ![Simulation Normal On.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/37881774490393) **Simulate**. → The seam tape is now being applied to the selected segment and being reinforced. ![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/37880795938457) ### ![Label.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/39591676972825) Provide the options for seam tape extension. _****_ 1. Click on the segment with seam tape applied with ![Seam Taping On.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/37880812122905) **Seam Taping** tool. 2. Set the**Extend** option in the Property Editor. **N****on****e** | Seam tape does not extend. ---|--- **To Outline** | Extend to the pattern outline. **To Seam Taping** | Extend to another seam tape area of ​​the intersected line. * The arrow highlighted on the segment indicates the direction from start to end. ****📝****Note:**** * When extending a seam tape to another seam taping, please make sure there is an intersected seam tape for reference. * If you apply Seam Taping Extend in the lower version (before ver 2024.2), both Start and End are assigned as To Outline in the higher version.
content_description: This page provides a step-by-step guide on using the Seam Taping tool to reinforce pattern edges against drooping during simulation in CLO 3D.

title: Can I cancel my subscription?
content: **Question** Can I cancel my paid subscription? Can I cancel my free trial? **Answer** You can cancel your trial or paid subscription through the [Subscription](https://www.clo3d.com/en/accounts/subscription) section of your account page. Even if you cancel immediately after starting the free trial and regular subscription, you can still use the CLO program until the expiration date. *Please note cancelation of the subscription after the renewal is non-refundable. *Deactivation (remote logout) doesn't cancel your subscription. **Step 1.** Sign in to your account via [clo3d.com](https://clo3d.com/en/) **Step 2.** Navigate to your Subscription page and click the "Cancel Subscription" button. [![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/40475986511257)](https://clo3d.com/en/) **Step 3.** Proceed with the survey for the cancelation reason and click the confirmation button. **Step 4.** Check the Billing section that your subscription expiration date. Please submit an inquiry through our [Contact Us](https://clo3d.com/en/support/contactus) page if you have any questions or difficulties.
content_description: Find out how to easily cancel your paid subscription or free trial through your account's Subscription page.

title: Set Color Theme
content: **New in CLO 2024.2. ** Set the theme to Dark or Light based on your preference and environment. **Dark theme** uses a dark background for the user interface, reducing eye strain and glare, especially in low-light environments. It helps to keep the overall brightness of the screen lower, which can be more comfortable during prolonged use. **Light theme** , on the other hand, features a bright background that provides a clean and crisp appearance, improving readability in well-lit environments. **** 1. Click on the **Setting » User Settings** in the menu bar. 2. Set the theme under **User Interface > Appearance**. ** ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/37041977442841) ****** 3. Restart CLO to apply the theme.
content_description: Discover how to customize your CLO 2024.2 experience by selecting between Dark and Light themes for optimal comfort and readability based on your environment.

title: Low-Res Garment
content: **List of Conetents** Low-Res Garment Low-Res Garment Settings **Low-Res Garment ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JQHYRWeRYls \- Decrease general quality of the 3D Garment. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022475628/mceclip0.png) **Low-Res Garment** tool from the 3D toolbar or navigate and select Main Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ **Low-Res Garment.** ** Low-Res Garment Settings ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ONAksiYyWLE \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022475648/mceclip1.png) **Low-Res Garment** tool from the 3D toolbar and the Low-Res Properties window will appear. * **Particle Distance** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7hjdc8LLbSs \- Change all Patterns’ Particle Distance to 20mm. \- Modify **Tolerance** to decide the range of Particle Distance so that only Patterns with corresponding Particle Distance value will be affected. Patterns with Particle Distance value outside of the **Tolerance** will not be affected. The default **Tolerance** range is 5mm to 20mm. * **Add’l Thickness - Collision** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=G6Gs7oZjx5k \- Change all Patterns’ Add’l Thickness- Collision to the default value, 2.5mm. \- Modify **Tolerance** to decide the range of Add’l Thickness- Collision so that only Patterns with corresponding Add’l Thickness - Collision value will be affected. Patterns with Add’l Thickness - Collision value outside of the Tolerance will not be affected. ** ** * **Skin Offset ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IvPi7Rh80YU \- Change all Avatar’s Skin Offset to the default value, 3mm. \- Modify **Tolerance** to decide the range of Skin Offset so that only Patterns with corresponding Skin Offset value will be affected. Patterns with Skin Offset value outside of the Tolerance will not be affected. * **Simulation Quality** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nBEg_qOqKgU \- Change the Simulation preset to the default setting, NORMAL. \- To decrease the general quality of the 3D Garment only with the desired options, toggle off options as needed. \- Select OK. The **Simulation** icon will change. \- Activate the **Simulation** to apply the settings. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: Explore essential tools and settings for optimizing the quality and performance of Low-Res Garments in 3D design.

title: Reset 3D Arrangement (All)
content: **Reset 3D Arrangement（All）** **YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zjnyrLjbaAk** \- Re-arrange 3D Patterns prior to the Simulation. \- Use the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022651728/mceclip1.png) **Reset 3D Arrangement(All)** tool when Garments are not properly draped after arranging them in the 3D window. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022651728/mceclip1.png) **Reset 3D Arrangement(All)** tool from the 3D toolbar. \- Or, navigate to the Main Menu and select 3D Garment ▶ **Reset 3D Arrangement(All). ** \- All Patterns will be re-arranged in the 3D window prior to the Simulation.

title: Reset 2D Arrangement (All)
content: **Reset 2D Arrangement（All）** **YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uHnRe1mwsco** **-** Re-Arrange 3D Patterns according to the Pattern Arrangement in the 2D window. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022651688/mceclip0.png) **Reset 2D Arrangement（All)** tool from the 3D toolbar. \- Or, navigate to the Main Menu and select 3D Garment ▶ **Reset 2D Arrangement (All).** \- All Patterns will be re-arranged in the 3D window reflecting the Pattern Arrangement in the 2D window.

title: Pleats
content: **Objective** Create the desired shape of pleats to Patterns. YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1RSYTLRsnzM ** Location** Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Pleats ▶ **Pleats**** **2D Toolbar ▶**![Pleats.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360059605713/Pleats.png) Pleats** **** **Operation** 1. Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. ** ** 2. Click to create a start point and an endpoint of a reference line of the pleats along Pattern Outlines. → A Pattern is divided into two. 3. Click on the side where the pleats will be added. → The Pleats window appears. 4. Configure the options and select OK. **Pleats Type** | Select the type of the pleats (Knife, Box, or Accordion). ---|--- ** Specification ** | Number of Pleats | Decide the number of pleats. Depth | Assign the depth of the pleats (the depth of folded pleats). Interval | Set the interval between pleats when there are two or more pleats. Create Notch | Select where to create Notch (Both, Start, or End). Reverse Direction | Reverse the direction where the pleats will be added. **Option** | Assign fold angles to the fold lines. Greater the difference between the angle of Outside Fold and Inside Fold, sharper the folds are. → The pleats are created on the Pattern. → If there is an Internal Line in the Pattern, it is also moved and rotated along with the Pattern. (ver 6.0) **※ Note: **If the segment where pleats to be created is sewn to another Pattern, the pleats will be automatically sewn. If the segment is not sewn, use the [Pleats Sewing](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000307468-%ED%94%8C%EB%A6%AC%EC%B8%A0-%EC%A0%91%EA%B8%B0-%EC%9E%AC%EB%B4%89) tool to sew the pleats to the other Pattern.
content_description: This web page serves as a comprehensive guide for creating and customizing pleats in 2D patterns using CLO 3D software.
